1.2.m: In what sacred field may that knowledge be attained, without studying scriptures and the like,

The intellect of all embodied beings does not engage at all

By the māhātmya of which place can embodied beings obtain pure knowledge
even through minor observances? Tell me of that place!

Because of their equal kinship [with him], the joy [of Menā and the Snow Mountain] increases exceedingly. // 33
Bearing matted locks perceived as hundreds of thousands of tree-shoots,

With the moon and sun standing on both sides of his luminous, water-rich peak,

In the rainy season, with a deep-blue cloud beneath his crest,
he shines as though bearing the Kālakūṭa poison at his throat. // 36
This lord of mountains, who has a thousand feet and a thousand heads,
is not merely declared by the Veda, but is also perceived directly with one's own eyes. // 37
That the stream of the river of the gods formerly rested upon his head is not wondrous;
even today, this Lord of the Mountain has hosts of numerous rivers resting upon his peaks. // 38
Having obtained slopes with autumn clouds,
he imitates [Śiva] mounted upon the foremost bull, the best of cattle. // 39
Where Nīlalohita clings closely to the tip of the peak—
he bears the state of Sthāṇu through being stationary, and terror (bhīmatā) through his dense forest (gahanatva); // 1.3.2.4.40
he also bears ferocity (ugratva) because of his extreme impassibility (sudurgamatva), not merely by name.
Where petty reptiles, having made their dwelling on the mountain slopes, // 41
vie with Takṣaka, Ananta, and other lords of serpents;
who, having manifested with eight corners all around by means of his powers (vibhūti), // 42
clearly defines, as it were, his own eightfold form (aṣṭamūrti);
the two rivers [flowing from] energy (śakti) are themselves the Iḍā and Piṅgalā, // 43
while in the middle, flowing from the peak of Śiva, the lotus-river is the Suṣumnā.
To see the base and the top of him whose nature is the pillar of fire, // 44
Brahmā and Viṣṇu, taking the forms of a boar and a swan, were not capable.
And prayed to by both of them, Śambhu established his presence there. // 45
Taking refuge [there] under the name Lord of Aruṇācala, along with his attendants,
there Gautama, the lord of yogins, for a thousand years // 46
performed severe austerities and brought Sadāśiva before his eyes.
The daughter of the Snowy Mountain also, having performed austerity there of old, // 47
obtained the left half of the body of the enemy of Manmatha when he was pleased.
Installed there by Gaurī under the name Lord of Pravālādri, // 48
the liṅga grants enjoyment to men and prepares [them] for absolute liberation.
There, by the command of Gaurī, Durgā, the slayer of Mahiṣa, // 49

Known there at Gaurī’s hermitage is a new [pool], the Khaḍgatīrtha; // 1.3.2.4.50

And the liṅga worshipped by Durgā, named Pāpanāśana, // 51

There King Vajrāṅgada, though rich in wealth, [fell] through transgression, // 52

Merely by circumambulating it, Kāntiśālin and Kalādhara, // 53
two lords of Vidyādharas, were released from the bondage of Durvāsas's curse.

Nandikeśvara said:
“A man endowed with the quality of pure sattva is rare in this world;
men endowed with the qualities of rajas and tamas are easily found. // 1
A person endowed with sattva, through a virtuous disposition, would attain the highest beatitude.
Because of the variety of these actions, for their experience, by the Creator
various hells indeed have been created here and there.
Experiencing [the hell] Mahāraurava, a donkey, a dog, or a pig,
or an outcaste after death, a man would become through killing a brahmin.
Imprisoned in Raurava for a long time, the state of a worm, insect, or moth
a twice-born man would attain, and [servile] manual labor, through drinking liquor.
From stealing the property of a brahmin, he would obtain the state of a brahmarākṣasa.
Whatever he steals, he would be bereft of that in another birth.
Having suffered torment in the Asipatravana hell for a very long time, again,
a man who violates his guru's bed would become a eunuch.
Tormented by the servants of Yama with heated iron rods,
the seducer of another's wife would dwell in the hell called Kālasūtra.
An arsonist would reside in Ghora; in Sughora, a poisoner.
In Mahāghora, a slanderer; and in Avīci, a reviler of dharma.
A betrayer of friends would dwell in Karāla; in Bhīma, one solely devoted to violence.
In Saṃhāra, a covert sinner; in Bhayānaka, a liar.
In Asighora would reside one who robs stepwells, wells, fields, men, and the like.
In Vajra, one intent on malice toward others; in Tarala, a meat-eating twice-born, [O sage].
In Tīkṣṇa, one who betrays mother and father; in Tāpana, one who corrupts mantra-recitation.
Even a killer of a horse would dwell in Nirucchvāsa; and a cow-killer in Dāruṇa.
An abortionist would dwell in Caṇḍa; a slayer of women in Kukūla.
A stealer of god's property [dwells] in Dahana; in Ghoraghora, a stealer of others' property.
The messengers of Yama in hell indeed [punish] all the sinners:
They bind them with ropes, strike them with clubs, pierce them with spikes.
Herons with sharp iron beaks, great serpents with cruel fangs,
dogs, tigers, and other beasts of prey bite them.
They hack them to pieces with weapons and burn their bodies.
They bury them in deep pits and beat them with whips.
They are cooked in caldrons of oil; they are pricked with fine needles.
Sinners are indeed forced to carry unendurable loads by Yama's messengers.
A killer of a brahmin becomes consumptive; a drinker of liquor has blackish teeth.
A gold thief has diseased nails; one who violates his guru's bed has skin disease.
A betrayer of a guru is epileptic; a reviler of the Vedas is an outcaste.
A false witness has eye disease; and one who eats before [others/offerings] has weak digestion.
One who steals knowledge becomes mute; a thief of books is blind.
One given to another's wife becomes lame; a slanderer of others is deaf.
One devoid of proper conduct becomes a cesspool swine, and a thief gets a tongue disease.
One who abandons an arrived guest gets boils on his cheeks.
One who has intercourse with women on festive days suffers from urinary disease; an eater of forbidden food has a foul mouth.
A violator of boundaries becomes a servant; an appropriator of tanks and pleasure gardens, a donkey.
One who fails to give what was promised becomes short-lived; a boaster becomes a dog.

Nandikeśvara said:
"I will explain today in detail the expiation of great sins
for all [people]; listen carefully, adopting a faithful mindset.
A killer of a brahmin, having reached the Crimson Mountain, bathed in the Khaḍgatīrtha,
reciting the five-syllable mantra, wearing holy ash and rudrākṣa beads,
having fasted, and worshiping the Supreme Lord with purity,
should feed brahmins for a year, eating alms, with his senses restrained.
He should perform special worship and service to the God with devotion.
Completely freed from [the sin of] killing a brahmin, he is glorified in the world of Brahmā.
Even a liquor drinker, residing for one year in the sacred field of Aruṇa,
having observed proper conduct as before and thus worshiping Maheśvara,
should bathe the God with milk while reciting the Śatarudrīya."
he is swiftly freed from the sin born of drinking liquor. (6)
One who commits the theft of gold, [if] in the sacred field of Śoṇa, having worshipped Hara with bilva leaves
and fed the learned brahmins, is freed from that formidable sin. (7)
One who has engaged in sexual relations with his guru's wife, going to Aruṇācala under [the constellation] Kṛttikā,
becoming an observer of vows as before, by means of a thousand lamps, (8)
having worshipped Śrī Śoṇācalaśaṃkara for three months,
should bestow an adorned maiden upon a wise brahmin. (9)
He should constantly repeat the six-syllabled mantra; thereby he is freed from sin,
and he dwells in the world of Śiva until the dissolution of worldly existence, without a doubt. (10)
And one who violates another man's wife, with restrained senses in this sacred field,
worshipping Aruṇaśaṃkara with fresh flowers for one month, (11)
should bestow wealth upon a devotee of Maheśvara according to his capacity.
At that very moment, he will be thoroughly freed from that sin. (12)
Even a poisoner, having observed vows in the sacred field of Aruṇa as previously described,
offering a gift of milk to the god, is freed from fault. (13)
Even a slanderer, observing vows in the sacred field of Aruṇa and devoted to the Vedas,
should instruct the foremost twice-born; then he becomes free of blemish. (14)
Even an arsonist, observing vows as before in the sacred field of Aruṇa for three months,
should build and offer a house to a devotee of Śiva for the pacification of that sin. (15)
One who reviles dharma, dwelling as a vrati in the sacred field of Śoṇa for a year,
should perform charitable distributions of food and the like to the best of his capacity for the pacification of sin. (16)
One who is malicious towards his father, remaining unwearied in the sacred field of Aruṇa for a month,
should give cows by the thousands to the Lord of the Mountain and to the twice-born. (17)
Having fed many twice-born at the times of planetary eclipses,
he should release a dark-colored bull; thereby he is freed from that sin. (18)
Even a murderer of a woman or a murderer of a child, having arrived at the sacred field of Śoṇa,
should give sesame seeds to the twice-born on a vyatīpāta day for the destruction of wicked deeds. (19)

O master Nandikeśvara, blissful through eternal Śiva, O lord!
I am delighted by you with the nectar of the majesty of the Lord of Śoṇa. / 1
How did Vajrāṅgada, the king of the Pāṇḍyas, commit a transgression
against Śoṇa, and how, through devotion to him alone, did he regain his prosperity? / 2
How were the two lords of the vidyādharas, Kāntiśālin and Kalādhara,
pierced by the curse of Durvāsas, protected by Śoṇa-Śambhu? / 3
Nandikeśvara said:
You have attained the fruition of your long life, O son of Mṛkaṇḍu,
since this steadfast devotion of yours is directed towards the Lord of beings. / 4
I shall tell the story of Vajrāṅgada and the account of the two vidyādharas,
from which the majesty of the Lord of Śoṇādri became celebrated in the world. / 5
Formerly, among the Pāṇḍyas, there was a king named Vajrāṅgada,
on the pillar of whose arm the earth rested like a bracket figure. / 6
Righteous, knowing justice, discerning, profound, courteous, forbearing,
calm, modest, wise, devoted to a single wife, accomplished, / 7
intent on worshipping and honoring Śiva, fortunate, foremost among the virtuous,
having conquered his enemies, he ruled the earth from the Bridge to Kedāra. / 8
Once, riding a fine horse under the pretext of hunting,
he entered deep into the dense forest bordering Aruṇācala. / 9
There, having seen a musk deer
diffusing a strong fragrance, he urged his horse after it out of curiosity. / 10
Pursued by him, that swift deer, having circumambulated
Śoṇaparvata clockwise, fell to the ground. / 11
Then the king, his strength broken and exhausted from riding,
fell from his mount, drained of luster, like one whose merit is exhausted falling from heaven. / 12
Afflicted in this way by an unknown cause, as though by an elephant,
the king, like one seized by a planet, did not know himself for a moment. / 13
And he thought: 'What is this causeless ruin of my courage?
Where has my riding horse suddenly gone?' / 14
While he was thus distraught with worry, unable to understand what had happened,
the sky suddenly appeared as if matted with banks of lightning. / 15
Even as he watched, shedding their animal bodies,
the horse and the deer quickly attained the state of sky-farers. / 16
Wearing diadems, earrings, necklaces, and armlets,

Mārkaṇḍeya said:
“O Lord, moon to the ocean of the māhātmya of the Lord,
O Nandīśa, the wonderful conduct of the two Vidyādharas has been heard. // 1
When did Vajrāṅgada attain perfection? How did he worship the God?
And how did the God, the Lord of Aruṇa, favor him who was bowed [in reverence]?” // 2
Nandikeśvara said:
Then, abandoning the desire to return towards his own city,
the king chose to dwell right at the foot of that [mountain]. // 3
Then his vast army, following the track of the mount,
crowded with chariots, elephants, horses, and foot-soldiers, arrived. // 4
The ruler of the earth, such an ocean of fortitude, was seen
by his royal chaplain, ministers, vassals, army commanders, and best of friends. // 5
Then, having honored that army which had arrived, the protector of the earth
stationed it entirely outside the boundary of Aruṇādri. // 6
His entire treasury, and also regions bearing great fruit,
the devoted king dedicated for the worship of the Lord of the Crimson Mountain. // 7
Having himself made a penance grove near the hermitage of Gautama,
instructed by his royal priest, together with his ministers, he became dedicated to the worship of Śiva. // 8
Having installed his son named Ratnāṅgada in his own post,
he propitiated the Lord of the Crimson [Mountain] with inexhaustible [tributes] sent by him. // 9
All around the Crimson Mountain, [endowed with] filled reservoirs of water,
he granted many fruitful agrahāras to the brahmins. // 10
By the power of the Lord of Aruṇa, who has the form of a pillar of fire,
in this land, though mostly arid, he constructed hundreds of oblong ponds. // 11
The far-sighted king offered the choice women of his own retinue,
endowed with beauty, for the service of the Lord of the Crimson [Mountain]. // 12
Then, by Agastya, who had arrived together with his companion Lopāmudrā,
he who was devoted to the worship of the Lord of the Crimson Mountain was praised. // 13
Every day performing ritual ablution in the lake named Navatīrtha,
he, self-restrained, worshipped Pāpanāśa and Pravāleśa. // 14
The ruler of men daily propitiated Durgā,
the slayer of the demon Mahiṣa, who removes afflictions from fortresses and difficulties. // 15
At every moment, of the one worthy of worship by Brahmā and Viṣṇu, who has the form of a liṅga,
he arranged various forms of worship for the primordial God.
Rising at dawn and having bathed, on foot alone the king
circumambulated three times, reciting the five-syllabled mantra.
On the full-moon day of Kārttika, pleasing to the beloved of Pārvatī,
he celebrated the Great Festival of Lamps, honoured throughout the three worlds.
Filled with water of sandalwood, white water-lilies, and camphor,
with thousands of golden vessels he bathed the Lord of the three yantras.
Preceded by the monthly raising of the flag and other festival rites at the sacred ford,
he conducted the grand chariot procession, revered across the three worlds.
With a pure heart, he also made a full bodily circumambulation
of the Crimson Mountain, which spans three yojanas in length.
Calling out, “O Lord of Aruṇācala! Ocean of the nectar of compassion!
O Lord who dwells with Aruṇā!” he praised him again and again.
Having smeared [him] daily with various substances such as the five nectars,
he anointed [him] with sandalwood paste pale with camphor.

1.2.m: “Fear not, my child! Good fortune to you. I possess eight forms;
they have all been fashioned for the highest welfare of all living beings.
Formerly, as Indra, you stood on the peak of Kailāsa,
and full of pride, you slighted me; then you were paralyzed by me.
Your pride melted away in an instant; ashamed of being paralyzed,
you then begged for the knowledge of Śiva, the cause of all sovereignty.
You were instructed by me: ‘O wielder of the thunderbolt, descending to the earth,
you shall become King Vajrāṅgada and attain my grace.’
By that power, this sacred field which is my abode was reached.

1.2.m: Ether, wind, fire, water, earth, the sun, the moon, and the individual soul—
through these forms of mine the whole universe of moving and unmoving things shines forth.
Indeed, as Time I impel all objects, living beings, and cosmic paths;
beyond the principles, I am Śiva; nothing here exists apart from me.
Certain waves rising up from me, the boundless ocean of consciousness and bliss,
are called Brahmā, Mukunda, Rudra, Indra, and the rest.
Speech, Lakṣmī, Patience, Faith, Wisdom, Svāhā, Svadhā, and others
are the powers of creation belonging to my immeasurable great power.
This Gaurī is my great power, Māyā, the mother of the universe;
by her the universe is constantly veiled, and it is also expanded.
Endowed with this power, performing the sport of creation, preservation, and dissolution,
by my own will I behold this multifaceted picture of the universe.
Free from delusion, contemplate my greatness
and realize yourself as non-different from me, like a wave from the ocean.”
Then, having attained sovereignty over the earth, full of my form,
by my grace, O king of kings, enjoy pleasures as you wish. (46)
Then, having long enjoyed divine happiness as Indra,
you shall assuredly attain oneness of form with me, O king. (47)
Nandikeśvara said:
Having spoken thus, when the god vanished, King Vajrāṅgada, successful,
worshipping Śoṇeśa alone, attained all pleasures. (48)
Thus has been recounted to you, O virtuous one, the glory of Śiva's devotee,
and the eternal fruit of circumambulating Śoṇa Mountain. (49)
What need of many words here? Circumambulation of Śoṇa Mountain
is superior even to a hundred great horse sacrifices. (50)
On the equinoxes, solstices, and conjunctions, at Vyatīpāta and other sacred occasions,
from circumambulating Śoṇa Mountain one obtains incalculable reward. (51)
There is no sacred field like Aruṇa; there is no deity like Aruṇeśvara;
nor is there found any austerity superior to circumambulation. (52)
While Nandikeśvara was speaking thus, the son of Mṛkaṇḍu, his whole body bristling with joy,
again and again weeping showers of tears of joy, seemed immersed in a great ocean of nectar. (53)

1.2.m: 11. Next, Viṣṇu, assuming the form of a boar, travels to the nether world to ascertain the lower limit of that luminous liṅga; having searched the lower part of the liṅga and determined that the liṅga is infinite, he turns back and returns to his previous place ... 245

1.2.s: 12 atha tasya tejomayaliṃgasyordhvāntaparyantaparicchittaye haṃsarūpadhāāriṇā brahmaṇa ūrdhvalokagamanam, tatra liṃgoparitanabhāgaśodhanapravṛttasya brahmaṇo'tidūra'ticirāgataketakīpatreṇa saha samāgamaḥ ... .245
1.2.d: 12 अथ तस्य तेजोमयलिंगस्योर्ध्वान्तपर्यन्तपरिच्छित्तये हंसरूपधाआरिणा ब्रह्मण ऊर्ध्वलोकगमनम्, तत्र लिंगोपरितनभागशोधनप्रवृत्तस्य ब्रह्मणोऽतिदूरऽतिचिरागतकेतकीपत्रेण सह समागमः ... .245
1.2.m: 12. Next, Brahmā, assuming the form of a swan, travels to the upper world to ascertain the upper limit of that luminous liṅga; there Brahmā, having set out to search the upper region of the liṅga, meets with a ketakī leaf that had fallen from very far and after a very long time ... .245

1.2.s: 13 atha mithyāsākṣyapradānāya prārthitena ketakīpatreṇa saha brahmaṇo mūlasthānaṃ pratyāgatya viṣṇave liṅgordhvaparyaṃtadarśanasya ketakīpatradvārā mithyāsākṣyeṇa satyāpanam 246
1.2.d: 13 अथ मिथ्यासाक्ष्यप्रदानाय प्रार्थितेन केतकीपत्रेण सह ब्रह्मणो मूलस्थानं प्रत्यागत्य विष्णवे लिङ्गोर्ध्वपर्यंतदर्शनस्य केतकीपत्रद्वारा मिथ्यासाक्ष्येण सत्यापनम् 246
1.2.m: 13. Next, Brahmā, returning to the original place together with the ketakī leaf requested to give false testimony, confirms to Viṣṇu through the false testimony of the ketakī leaf that he had seen the upper limit of the liṅga 246

1.2.s: 14 atha viṣṇunā hṛdayena tadasatyaṃ viniścitya svātmarakṣārthaṃ brahmaṇaśca madanivṛttaye tejomayaliṃgasvarūpasya bhagavataḥ stutikaraṇam. ... 246
1.2.d: 14 अथ विष्णुना हृदयेन तदसत्यं विनिश्चित्य स्वात्मरक्षार्थं ब्रह्मणश्च मदनिवृत्तये तेजोमयलिंगस्वरूपस्य भगवतः स्तुतिकरणम्. ... 246
1.2.m: 14. Next, Viṣṇu, discerning in his heart that it is false, for the sake of protecting himself and removing Brahmā's arrogance, offers praise to the Lord whose nature is the luminous liṅga. ... 246

1.2.s: 15 atha viṣṇukṛtastutyā prasannena śaṃkareṇa tejaḥstaṃbhaṃ vinirbhidya saguṇapañcavadanamūrtiprakaṭanam, taṃ saguṇarūpaṃ parameśvaraṃ śrīśaṃkaraṃ dṛṣṭvā viṣṇorānandaḥ,tathā ca brahmaṇo lajjāprāptiḥ, maheśvareṇa brahmaṇe'pūjyatārūpaśāpapradānam, ketakacchadasya ca svapūjānarhatārūpaśāpapradānam, atha brahmadevakṛtaśivastutyudyamaḥ 247
1.2.d: 15 अथ विष्णुकृतस्तुत्या प्रसन्नेन शंकरेण तेजःस्तंभं विनिर्भिद्य सगुणपञ्चवदनमूर्तिप्रकटनम्, तं सगुणरूपं परमेश्वरं श्रीशंकरं दृष्ट्वा विष्णोरानन्दः,तथा च ब्रह्मणो लज्जाप्राप्तिः, महेश्वरेण ब्रह्मणेऽपूज्यतारूपशापप्रदानम्, केतकच्छदस्य च स्वपूजानर्हतारूपशापप्रदानम्, अथ ब्रह्मदेवकृतशिवस्तुत्युद्यमः 247
1.2.m: 15. Next, Śaṃkara, pleased by the praise offered by Viṣṇu, splits open the pillar of fire and reveals his five-faced form endowed with attributes; Viṣṇu's joy upon seeing that supreme lord, glorious Śaṃkara, in his form with attributes, and likewise Brahmā's experiencing shame; the bestowal of a curse of unworthiness of worship upon Brahmā by Maheśvara, and the bestowal of a curse upon the ketakī leaf of being unfit for his worship; then, Brahmā's preparation to offer praise to Śiva 247

1.2.s: 16 atha brahmadevena śivastutikaraṇam, evaṃ brahmaviṣṇustutiprasannena bhagavatā śrīśaṃkareṇa brahmaviṣṇvorvarapradānapūrvakaṃ punaḥ svādhikārapālanārthamājñākaraṇam ,śrīśoṇācale'vasthityarthamājñākaraṇaṃ ca, tato bhagavadantardhānānantaraṃ brahmaviṣṇubhyāṃ śrīśoṇācale saraḥ khananapūrvakamaruṇapuranirmāṇapuraḥsarāruṇācaleśvaramandiranirmāṇam- .. 248
1.2.d: 16 अथ ब्रह्मदेवेन शिवस्तुतिकरणम्, एवं ब्रह्मविष्णुस्तुतिप्रसन्नेन भगवता श्रीशंकरेण ब्रह्मविष्ण्वोर्वरप्रदानपूर्वकं पुनः स्वाधिकारपालनार्थमाज्ञाकरणम् ,श्रीशोणाचलेऽवस्थित्यर्थमाज्ञाकरणं च, ततो भगवदन्तर्धानानन्तरं ब्रह्मविष्णुभ्यां श्रीशोणाचले सरः खननपूर्वकमरुणपुरनिर्माणपुरःसरारुणाचलेश्वरमन्दिरनिर्माणम्- .. 248
1.2.m: 16. Next, the offering of praise to Śiva by Brahmā; then the Lord, glorious Śaṃkara, pleased with the praise of Brahmā and Viṣṇu, after granting boons to Brahmā and Viṣṇu, commands them to observe their authorities again and commands them to dwell on glorious Śoṇa Mountain; then, after the Lord's disappearance, Brahmā and Viṣṇu dig a lake on glorious Śoṇa Mountain, construct Aruṇapura, and build the temple of the Lord of Aruṇācala- .. 248

1.2.s: 17 atha śivapārvatyorvihāravarṇanam, kṛtasya tapaso vṛttāntavarṇane tatra cānekacaritapuraḥsaraṃ caturmukhanārāyaṇayorherambaṣaḍānanatvādivṛttāntavarṇanam ... 249
1.2.d: 17 अथ शिवपार्वत्योर्विहारवर्णनम्, कृतस्य तपसो वृत्तान्तवर्णने तत्र चानेकचरितपुरःसरं चतुर्मुखनारायणयोर्हेरम्बषडाननत्वादिवृत्तान्तवर्णनम् ... 249
1.2.m: 17. Now the description of the sporting of Śiva and Pārvatī; in the narration of the account of the austerity performed, preceded by various deeds there, the narration of the account of the four-faced Brahmā and Nārāyaṇa becoming Heramba and the six-faced [Skanda], and so forth... 249

1.2.s: 18 atha praṇayakopakupitāyāḥ pārvatyāḥ śivasakāśato niṣkramya nijadehakālimanivṛttaye tapaḥkaraṇārthaṃ sakhībhiḥ saha gautamāśramaṃ pratyāgamanam, atha gautamopadeśena devyā tadāśramasamīpe tīvrataraniyamadhāraṇapūrvakamanudinamaruṇācaleśvaraparicaraṇarūpatapaḥkaraṇam 249
1.2.d: 18 अथ प्रणयकोपकुपितायाः पार्वत्याः शिवसकाशतो निष्क्रम्य निजदेहकालिमनिवृत्तये तपःकरणार्थं सखीभिः सह गौतमाश्रमं प्रत्यागमनम्, अथ गौतमोपदेशेन देव्या तदाश्रमसमीपे तीव्रतरनियमधारणपूर्वकमनुदिनमरुणाचलेश्वरपरिचरणरूपतपःकरणम् 249
1.2.m: 18. Now the arrival of Pārvatī, angered by lovers' quarrel, leaving Śiva's presence to go to the hermitage of Gautama along with her female companions in order to perform austerity for the removal of the dark complexion of her own body; then, by the instruction of Gautama, the Goddess's performance of austerity in the form of daily service to the Lord of Aruṇācala near that hermitage, while observing exceedingly severe vows... 249

1.2.s: 19 atha tatra tapaḥsthitāyā devyā lobhanārthaṃ mahiṣāsureṇa nijapraśaṃsānivedanāya devīṃ prati dūtīpreṣaṇama, devīsakhyā mahiṣāsuradūtyāṃ tataḥ sthānānnisāritāyāṃ mahiṣāsurasya mahatā sainyena saha devīṃ pratyāgamanam, atha devyā mahiṣāsurasainyakolāhalaṃ śrutvā daityasaṃhārārthaṃ durgāṃ pratyājñākaraṇam, durgādevyā svāṃgebhyo vividhayoginīcakramātṛkādisainyanirmāṇama, tato devīsainyadaityasainyayostumuladvandvayuddhavarṇanam, tato mahiṣāsurasyājayyatāṃ dṛṣṭvā mātṛkādibhirdurgādevīstutikaraṇam, tato durgādevyā mahiṣāsureṇa saha saṃgrāme durgādevīkṛtamahiṣāsuravadhavṛttāntavarṇanam. -. 251
1.2.d: 19 अथ तत्र तपःस्थिताया देव्या लोभनार्थं महिषासुरेण निजप्रशंसानिवेदनाय देवीं प्रति दूतीप्रेषणम, देवीसख्या महिषासुरदूत्यां ततः स्थानान्निसारितायां महिषासुरस्य महता सैन्येन सह देवीं प्रत्यागमनम्, अथ देव्या महिषासुरसैन्यकोलाहलं श्रुत्वा दैत्यसंहारार्थं दुर्गां प्रत्याज्ञाकरणम्, दुर्गादेव्या स्वांगेभ्यो विविधयोगिनीचक्रमातृकादिसैन्यनिर्माणम, ततो देवीसैन्यदैत्यसैन्ययोस्तुमुलद्वन्द्वयुद्धवर्णनम्, ततो महिषासुरस्याजय्यतां दृष्ट्वा मातृकादिभिर्दुर्गादेवीस्तुतिकरणम्, ततो दुर्गादेव्या महिषासुरेण सह संग्रामे दुर्गादेवीकृतमहिषासुरवधवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्. -. 251
1.2.m: 19. Now the sending of a female messenger to the Goddess by Mahiṣāsura to declare his own praise in order to entice the Goddess engaged in austerity there; when the female messenger of Mahiṣāsura was driven away from that place by the Goddess's companion, the arrival of Mahiṣāsura toward the Goddess with a vast army; then the Goddess, hearing the uproar of Mahiṣāsura's army, giving command to Durgā for the destruction of the demon; the goddess Durgā's creation of an army comprising various yoginī-cakras, mātṛkās, and others from her own limbs; then the description of the tumultuous single combat between the Goddess's army and the demon's army; then, seeing Mahiṣāsura's invincibility, the praising of the goddess Durgā by the mātṛkās and others; then, in the battle of the goddess Durgā with Mahiṣāsura, the description of the account of the slaying of Mahiṣāsura carried out by the goddess Durgā... 251

1.2.s: 20 atha durgāhaste mahiṣāsuramastakesaṃlagnatāyāṃ devyā upadeśena durgayā khaḍgena śilāpaṭṭapāṭanapūrvakaṃ khaḍgatīrthaṃ nirmāya tatra nimajjanam, tannimajjanasamaye mahiṣāsurakaṇṭha-sthitaliṅgapatanam, tasya liṅgasya pāpanāśanasaṃjñayā khaṅgatīrthatīre sthāpanam, tato durgādevyā hastāttasmāttīrthādunmajjanasamaye mahiṣāsuramastakapatanam, atha pārvatyā durgādevyai śivabhaktamahiṣāsurahananārthaṃ nijānumatipradānātpāpaśaṅkāprāptyanantaraṃ pāpāpanodāya prāyaścittajijñāsayā gautamaprārthanam, tato gautamena kārtikapūrṇimāyāmaruṇā caleśvarajyotirdarśanaparyantaṃ tapaścaryākaraṇārthamupadeśakaraṇam, atha gautamopadeśena pārvatyā tapaścaryākaraṇam, tataḥ kārtikapaurṇamāsyāṃ dināṃte śrīśoṇācalaśikhare jyotirdṛṣṭvā pārvatyā śrīśoṇādrīśvarastutikaraṇam, atha tatkṛtastutisaṃtuṣṭena bhagavatā sadyaḥ susvarūparūpadarśanapūrvakaṃ jagadambāyāḥ pārvatyāḥ sāntvanavarṇanam. ... 253
1.2.d: 20 अथ दुर्गाहस्ते महिषासुरमस्तकेसंलग्नतायां देव्या उपदेशेन दुर्गया खड्गेन शिलापट्टपाटनपूर्वकं खड्गतीर्थं निर्माय तत्र निमज्जनम्, तन्निमज्जनसमये महिषासुरकण्ठ-स्थितलिङ्गपतनम्, तस्य लिङ्गस्य पापनाशनसंज्ञया खङ्गतीर्थतीरे स्थापनम्, ततो दुर्गादेव्या हस्तात्तस्मात्तीर्थादुन्मज्जनसमये महिषासुरमस्तकपतनम्, अथ पार्वत्या दुर्गादेव्यै शिवभक्तमहिषासुरहननार्थं निजानुमतिप्रदानात्पापशङ्काप्राप्त्यनन्तरं पापापनोदाय प्रायश्चित्तजिज्ञासया गौतमप्रार्थनम्, ततो गौतमेन कार्तिकपूर्णिमायामरुणा चलेश्वरज्योतिर्दर्शनपर्यन्तं तपश्चर्याकरणार्थमुपदेशकरणम्, अथ गौतमोपदेशेन पार्वत्या तपश्चर्याकरणम्, ततः कार्तिकपौर्णमास्यां दिनांते श्रीशोणाचलशिखरे ज्योतिर्दृष्ट्वा पार्वत्या श्रीशोणाद्रीश्वरस्तुतिकरणम्, अथ तत्कृतस्तुतिसंतुष्टेन भगवता सद्यः सुस्वरूपरूपदर्शनपूर्वकं जगदम्बायाः पार्वत्याः सान्त्वनवर्णनम्. ... 253
1.2.m: 20. Now, when Mahiṣāsura's head remained stuck to Durgā's hand, Durgā, by the instruction of the Goddess, splitting a stone slab with her sword, fashioning the Khaḍgatīrtha, and immersing herself there; at the time of that immersion, the falling of the liṅga situated on Mahiṣāsura's neck; the installation of that liṅga on the bank of the Khaḍgatīrtha under the name Pāpanāśana; then, at the moment of emerging from that tīrtha, the falling of Mahiṣāsura's head from the hand of the goddess Durgā; now Pārvatī, after experiencing apprehension of sin due to granting her own assent to the goddess Durgā for the slaying of Mahiṣāsura who was a devotee of Śiva, supplicating Gautama with the desire to know the expiation for expelling the sin; then Gautama imparting instruction to perform the practice of austerities until the darśana of the light of the Lord of Aruṇācala on the full moon day of Kārtika; now Pārvatī's performance of the practice of austerities according to the instruction of Gautama; then, seeing the light on the summit of the venerable Śoṇācala at the end of the day on the full moon of Kārtika, Pārvatī's praising of the Lord of the venerable Śoṇa Mountain; then the description of the Lord, pleased by the praise offered by her, consoling Pārvatī, the Mother of the Universe, by immediately granting darśana of his auspicious own form... 253

1.2.s: 21 atha śrīśaṅkareṇa jagadambāyāḥ praśaṃsāpūrvakaṃ pārśve niveśanam, stanyārthinaṃ skandaṃ vihāya tapo'rthaṃ pārvatyāḥ śivasakāśato nirgamanakāraṇācchrīśaṃkareṇa jagadambāyāṃ apītakuceti nāmakaraṇam, mahiṣāsuramardinyā durgāyāḥ śrījagadambāsamīpe'vasthānam, khaḍgatīrthasya gautamamaharṣeḥ saptamātṛkādīnāṃ ca śrīśaṅkareṇa varapradānavarṇanam 254
1.2.d: 21 अथ श्रीशङ्करेण जगदम्बायाः प्रशंसापूर्वकं पार्श्वे निवेशनम्, स्तन्यार्थिनं स्कन्दं विहाय तपोऽर्थं पार्वत्याः शिवसकाशतो निर्गमनकारणाच्छ्रीशंकरेण जगदम्बायां अपीतकुचेति नामकरणम्, महिषासुरमर्दिन्या दुर्गायाः श्रीजगदम्बासमीपेऽवस्थानम्, खड्गतीर्थस्य गौतममहर्षेः सप्तमातृकादीनां च श्रीशङ्करेण वरप्रदानवर्णनम् 254
1.2.m: 21. Now the placing of the Mother of the Universe at his side by the venerable Śaṃkara after praising her; because Pārvatī had departed from Śiva's presence for the sake of austerity leaving behind Skanda who was seeking her breast, the venerable Śaṃkara giving the Mother of the Universe the name Apītakucā; Durgā, the slayer of Mahiṣāsura, remaining near the venerable Mother of the Universe; the description of the conferring of boons by the venerable Śaṃkara upon the Khaḍgatīrtha, the great sage Gautama, and the Seven Mothers and others... 254

1.2.s: 22 atha pāṇḍyadeśīya sārvabhauma vajrāṃgada bhūpāla caritra varṇanam, tatra vajrāṃgadasya hayamāruhya mṛgamanu śoṇācalaṃ gatasya madhyemārgaṃ vāhātpatanam, turaṅgasya kastūrīmṛgasya cetyubhayorapi śoṇādrau dehapatanena tatkṣaṇa eva maraṇānkhecaratvaprāptiḥ, atha rājñā pṛṣṭayostayoḥ khecarayorvidyādharayormadhye kāntiśālinā vidyādhareṇa vajrāṃgadāyātmano durvāsaḥśāpakāraṇakathanaprasaṃgena śrīśoṇaśailapradakṣiṇāmāhātmyakathanam, tatra śrīśoṇādrīśena śambhunā nijapradakṣiṇāṃ kṛtavate herambāya phalapradānapūrvakaṃ svasya śrīśoṇādrīśvarasya pradakṣiṇāmāhātmyakathanam - --- --. 254
1.2.d: 22 अथ पाण्ड्यदेशीय सार्वभौम वज्रांगद भूपाल चरित्र वर्णनम्, तत्र वज्रांगदस्य हयमारुह्य मृगमनु शोणाचलं गतस्य मध्येमार्गं वाहात्पतनम्, तुरङ्गस्य कस्तूरीमृगस्य चेत्युभयोरपि शोणाद्रौ देहपतनेन तत्क्षण एव मरणान्खेचरत्वप्राप्तिः, अथ राज्ञा पृष्टयोस्तयोः खेचरयोर्विद्याधरयोर्मध्ये कान्तिशालिना विद्याधरेण वज्रांगदायात्मनो दुर्वासःशापकारणकथनप्रसंगेन श्रीशोणशैलप्रदक्षिणामाहात्म्यकथनम्, तत्र श्रीशोणाद्रीशेन शम्भुना निजप्रदक्षिणां कृतवते हेरम्बाय फलप्रदानपूर्वकं स्वस्य श्रीशोणाद्रीश्वरस्य प्रदक्षिणामाहात्म्यकथनम् - --- --. 254
1.2.m: 22. Now the description of the deeds of King Vajrāṅgada, sovereign of the Pāṇḍya country; there, Vajrāṅgada, mounted on a horse and pursuing a deer toward Śoṇācala, falling from his mount midway on the road; both the horse and the musk-deer attaining the state of sky-wanderers immediately upon death due to their bodies falling on Śoṇādri; now, between the two sky-wandering vidyādharas questioned by the king, the description of the māhātmya of circumambulating the venerable Śoṇa Mountain by the radiant vidyādhara for Vajrāṅgada on the occasion of narrating the cause of his curse from Durvāsas; there, the description of the māhātmya of the circumambulation of himself, the Lord of the venerable Śoṇa Mountain, by Śambhu, the Lord of the venerable Śoṇa Mountain, preceded by conferring the fruit upon Heramba who circumambulated him... 254

1.2.s: 23 atha kalādharākhyena vidyādhareṇa vajrāṃgadāya bhūpataye nijaśāpavṛttāntanivedanam, atha kāntiśālikalādharayorvidyādharayorupadeśena vajrāṃgadabhūpasya śrīmadaruṇācalabhaktiviṣaye dṛḍhaniścayakaraṇam-
1.2.d: 23 अथ कलाधराख्येन विद्याधरेण वज्रांगदाय भूपतये निजशापवृत्तान्तनिवेदनम्, अथ कान्तिशालिकलाधरयोर्विद्याधरयोरुपदेशेन वज्रांगदभूपस्य श्रीमदरुणाचलभक्तिविषये दृढनिश्चयकरणम्-
1.2.m: 23. Now the recounting of the account of his own curse to King Vajrāṅgada by the vidyādhara named Kalādhara; now King Vajrāṅgada forming a firm resolve regarding devotion to the venerable Aruṇācala by the instruction of the two vidyādharas, Kāntiśālin and Kalādhara...

1.2.s:
24 atha vajrāṃgadabhūpatinā śrīmadaruṇācalasevārthaṃ nijasarvasaṃpattyupayogena brāhmaṇebhyo
vividhāgrahārādisamarpaṇapūrvakaṃ gautamaśramasamīpe nijatapovanaṃ vidhāya sarvatīrtha snāna sarvadevapūjāpūrvakaśivārcākaraṇam, vajrāṃgadakṛtayā tapaścaryayā saṃtuṣṭena bhagavatā vajrāṃgadāya nijamahimopadeśapūrvakavarapradānam ' bhagavadvaraprasādena vajrāṃgadasya sarvabhogāvāptipūrvakasadgativarṇanam, aruṇācaleśvarasya sarvātiśāyiśraiṣṭhyamāhātmya varṇanapūrvakamaruṇācalamāhātmyasamāptivarṇanam 256
1.2.d:
24 अथ वज्रांगदभूपतिना श्रीमदरुणाचलसेवार्थं निजसर्वसंपत्त्युपयोगेन ब्राह्मणेभ्यो
विविधाग्रहारादिसमर्पणपूर्वकं गौतमश्रमसमीपे निजतपोवनं विधाय सर्वतीर्थ स्नान सर्वदेवपूजापूर्वकशिवार्चाकरणम्, वज्रांगदकृतया तपश्चर्यया संतुष्टेन भगवता वज्रांगदाय निजमहिमोपदेशपूर्वकवरप्रदानम् ' भगवद्वरप्रसादेन वज्रांगदस्य सर्वभोगावाप्तिपूर्वकसद्गतिवर्णनम्, अरुणाचलेश्वरस्य सर्वातिशायिश्रैष्ठ्यमाहात्म्य वर्णनपूर्वकमरुणाचलमाहात्म्यसमाप्तिवर्णनम् 256
1.2.m: 24. Now King Vajrāṅgada, utilizing his entire wealth for the worship of the venerable Aruṇācala, making his own penance grove near Gautama's hermitage by first gifting various agrahāras and other grants to brahmins, and performing the worship of Śiva preceded by bathing in all tīrthas and worship of all deities; the Lord, pleased by the practice of austerities performed by Vajrāṅgada, conferring a boon upon Vajrāṅgada preceded by instruction regarding his own majesty; by the grace of the Lord's boon, the description of Vajrāṅgada's attainment of a good destiny preceded by the attainment of all enjoyments; the description of the conclusion of the Aruṇācalamāhātmya preceded by the description of the supreme and surpassing māhātmya of the Lord of Aruṇācala... 256
Thus ends the second half of the Aruṇācalamāhātmya, the third [part] in the Māheśvarakhaṇḍa. (13–23).
Thus ends the first, the Māheśvarakhaṇḍa, in the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa. || 1
